text: Ancient Egypt. Slaves build the pyramids.
Nope. Probably not.
Pyramids: the slaves myth.
In 1990, archaeologists found the workers' tombs.
Right next to the pyramids.
Slaves wouldn't be buried that close to the king.
Some tombs had bread and beer for the afterlife.
Skeletons show broken bones that healed.
So they got medical care.
Nearby was a whole workers' town.
Bakeries. Breweries. Lots of meat.
Work crews even gave themselves names.
Like "Friends of Khufu."
Many workers came in rotating shifts.
Some were probably drafted. But slaves? Unlikely.
So where did the slave idea come from?
Ancient Greek writers, and Hollywood movies.
Pyramid builders: skilled crews.
Evidence of slave armies: none found.
Anyway, here's the movie version.
